opening_vo.text: I like to focus on the sensation.
It's quite a tremendous thing, how you can just snuff it out.
It feels like, I don't know
like being at a beautiful beach with the birds and the sea.
That's how it feels like, I focus on that.

voicemail.text:
I called but you didn't pick up.
I guess you're sleeping again.

Uh… your father sent you
some money.

So… yeah. If you ever need
extra money, just call.

You can call the house too.
Johan will probably answer.

I sent Erika home
for a few days.

So yeah. You can tell your father,
or just call his cell.

Anyway, he also said —
I know you don't want to hear this —

But he wants to talk about you
maybe joining the company someday.

We both really think
you'd fit in there.

Karl is retiring soon,
so maybe… you know…

newspaper.text: "TWO KILLED IN STABBING ATTACKS ON LINNÉGATAN"

"Two people have been killed in separate stabbing attacks
on Linnégatan during the past two weeks."

"First, a homeless man in his 50s was found seriously injured
outdoors late in the evening and later died
from his injuries at the hospital."

"Earlier this week, a young girl who was reportedly
begging in the area was found dead
near a building entrance."

"Police are investigating the cases and examining
whether there is any connection between the incidents,"
"but no suspect has been arrested yet."

cafe_dialogue.text:
I don't get that stubborn idea that we have
to marry our – our job and our happiness.

I mean, you do something
to make a living because…
you're good at it, or like –
good enough at it to earn money,
because this is a consumer world,
you need money to live, that's it.

And that thing doesn't have to be
what gives you meaning.

When I was growing up
everyone always said:
"you have to work with something you love,"
or lawyers actually love their jobs?
Sure, you can love your job,
I find a lot of joy in it,
but the thing that really gives me meaning
is like making music or drawing,

and it's not really the same thing –
I don't know.

penulti_part1.text:
how you can kind of slide into a role
without really noticing it.

You wake up, do what you're supposed to,
say the right things, smile at the right moments.

It's not fake exactly.
Just… rehearsed.

And suddenly you're good at it.
Almost too good.

And I don't mean it's tragic.
It's not tragic.
You become efficient at being yourself.
Or, well, a version of yourself.

I used to think everything
had to hold together.

That what you feel inside and what you do
on the outside should match perfectly,

Maybe it's okay if there's
a space in between.

ending_vo.text: No that was a week before.

And, what did you-
did you just leave--

That was really close to the Slottsskogen.
So I just went there, to the marsh.
It's not really how you guys think it is.
It's not like a compulsion really.
So you just keep doing it.
